The '''2016–17 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team''' represented [[Indiana University (Bloomington)|Indiana University]] in the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. Their head coach was [[Tom Crean (basketball)|Tom Crean]], in what would be his final season in Bloomington. The team played its home games at [[Assembly Hall (Bloomington)|Simon Skjodt Assembly Hall]] in [[Bloomington, Indiana]], as a member of the [[Big Ten Conference]].

Despite the highs of the previous season and being ranked as high as No. 3 in the nation, the Hoosiers faced a troubling and disappointing year; they finished 18–16 overall and 7–11 in [[2016–17 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten]] play to finish in a tie for 10th place. At the [[2017 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]] they defeated [[2016–17 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|Iowa]] in the second round to advance to the quarterfinals, where they lost to [[2016–17 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]]. The Hoosiers missed out on the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] and lost in the first round of the [[2017 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]], their first appearance since 2005, to [[2016–17 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]]. The game was played at [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]]'s [[McCamish Pavilion]] because Indiana Athletic Director Fred Glass declined to host a home game at Simon Skjodt Assembly Hall, citing concerns it would "devalue" the Hoosiers' home court.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/early-lead/wp/2017/03/15/indiana-didnt-want-to-devalue-its-home-court-by-hosting-an-nit-game/|title=Indiana didn't want to 'devalue' its home court by hosting an NIT game|website=Washington Post|access-date=2017-03-16}}</ref>

On March 16, 2017, Indiana fired Crean after nine years as head coach.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tom Crean fired by Indiana|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2017/03/16/tom-crean-fired-indiana-basketball-coach|work=SI.com|access-date=March 16, 2017|date=March 16, 2017}}</ref> On March 25, 2017, the school hired [[Archie Miller (basketball)|Archie Miller]] as head coach.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/19001709/archie-miller-coach-indiana-hoosiers|title=Hoosiers hire Dayton's Archie Miller as coach|date=March 25, 2017|publisher=ESPN.com|last2=Katz|first2=Andy|first1=Jeff|last1=Goodman|author-link2=Andy Katz|access-date=March 25, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/indiana/2017/03/25/report-archie-miller-new-iu-coach/99618342/|title=Archie Miller 'a great hire for IU, great hire for the state'|work=Indianapolis Star|access-date=2017-03-27|language=en}}</ref>

==Previous season==
The [[2015–16 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Hoosiers]] finished the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16 season]] with a record 27–8, 15–3 in [[2015–16 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to win the Big Ten regular season title outright, pushing the school's total to 22 conference titles (tied with conference rival, [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]], for the most). They received the No. 1 seed in the [[2016 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], where they made an early quarterfinals exit by losing to [[2015-16 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]]. The team received a No. 5 seed in the NCAA Tournament, and defeated Chattanooga and Kentucky, having won two games before being eliminated in the Sweet 16 by North Carolina.

===Recruiting class===
Indiana was able to land its top recruit in De'Ron Davis, when he announced his commitment to become a Hoosier on November 12, 2015. IU had aggressively pursued Davis for more than three years, and they eventually beat out [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State]] for the highly touted 6'9 forward from Aurora, Colorado. After leading [[Overland High School]] to two consecutive 5A state championship titles, Davis was crowned 2016 Colorado Mr. Basketball.<ref name=davis>{{cite web|last=Bozich|first=Alex|title=De’Ron Davis named 2016 Colorado Mr. Basketball|url=http://www.insidethehall.com/2016/04/03/deron-davis-named-2016-colorado-mr-basketball/|work=Inside the Hall|access-date=April 3, 2016|date=April 3, 2016}}</ref>

On April 24, 2016, a fifth man was added to the recruiting class when JUCO transfer Freddie McSwain Jr. committed to play for IU. He hails from [[Hinesville, Georgia]] and played basketball at [[Neosho County Community College]].<ref name=mcswain>{{cite web|last=Bozich|first=Alex|title=JUCO forward Freddie McSwain joins IU’s 2016 recruiting class|url=http://www.insidethehall.com/2016/04/24/juco-forward-freddie-mcswain-joins-ius-2016-recruiting-class/|work=Inside the Hall|access-date=April 26, 2016|date=April 24, 2016}}</ref>
